docTitle: Your index exists. Your database ignores it.

slides.title:
Your index exists.
Your database
==ignores== it.
slides.sub: 2 reasons Postgres skips your index, 1 index it never creates for you, and how to check.

slides.title:
First, ask
the database
slides.lede: You added an index on email. Put EXPLAIN in front of the slow query.

panels.verdict:
Seq Scan = every row read.
Index Scan or Bitmap Index Scan = index used.

slides.tag: MySQL: ALL = full scan; ref/range = index.

slides.title:
Mistake 1:
a function on
the column
slides.lede: The index stores emails as they are.
slides.tag: MySQL's default collation ignores case, so LOWER() is rarely needed.

slides.title:
Mistake 2:
a wildcard
at the start

lines: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

slides.tag: Prefix only ('fall%')? A B-tree with text_pattern_ops works.

slides.title:
The index Postgres
never made for you
slides.lede: MySQL (InnoDB) creates an index on a foreign key column for you. PostgreSQL doesn't.
slides.takeaway: A common reason joins suddenly get slow after a move to Postgres.
slides.tag: Live table? Add CONCURRENTLY (no write lock).

slides.title:
When to add
an index

rows.head: Searched often
rows.sub: In WHERE, JOIN or ORDER BY.

rows.head: EXPLAIN shows a full scan
rows.sub: On a query that is slow.

rows.head: Not on every column
rows.sub: A table with 6 indexes: 1 row + 6 indexes = 7 writes per insert.

rows.head: Not on tiny tables
rows.sub: With about 10 rows, the database scans anyway.

slides.foot: Every index speeds up some reads and *slows down every insert*.
